source_text: Tu vero iustificasti, ut Propheta ait, sororem tuam Sodomam [n315] ; absolvi putabitur Manichaeus, si tuis blasphemiis comparetur. Gloriatus in primo operis mei libro fueram, quod eo ore lacerarer, quo et Apostoli iniuriam pertulissent; nunc vero expavesco magnitudinem felicitatis meae; ab eo vituperor, qui criminatur Deum.
pass_a_gloss: You however have justified, as the Prophet says, your sister Sodom; the Manichaean will be thought absolved, if he is compared with your blasphemies. I had gloried in the first book of my work, that I was lacerated by that mouth, by which the Apostles also had borne injury; now however I panic at the magnitude of my happiness; I am vituperated by him, who charges God.

lemmas.lexica: Blaise Manichaeus; Julian's polemic label vs natural evil

pass_b_english: You, however, have “justified your sister Sodom”, as the prophet says (Ezekiel 16:48, 51, 55). The Manichaean will seem acquitted if compared with your blasphemies. In the first book of my work I had boasted that I was attacked by the mouth from which the apostles too had suffered injury. Now I am awed by the greatness of my good fortune: I am reviled by someone who brings charges against God.

choices.why: Julian's standing charge: natural evil is Manichaean. Keep the sect-name, not 'dualists'.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
